Hi Tara — great to meet you earlier today. Thanks for the thoughtful discovery session. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

- What we heard from your team:
  - Primary use case: customer support automation (inbound triage + suggested replies) integrated into your support console.
  - Sensitive data: some PHI elements may appear in messages for certain workflows; you flagged this for security/legal review.
  - Decision criteria: data isolation, audit logs, SLAs for latency, and a clear procurement path for entitlements.

- Proposed immediate next steps:
  1) Stakeholder mapping: can you confirm the economic buyer and procurement contact? You mentioned Grace Lee (CFO) on the call — is she the final sign-off?
  2) Security intake: please share the security questionnaire and I'll route to our SE for intake.
  3) Schedule a 30-45 minute security kickoff next week to align scope (systems in/out, data flows, controls).

Attendees from our side: myself (AE), Neha Kapoor (Solutions Engineer) to run the questionnaire intake, and Rishi Malhotra (Sales Manager) to assist on contracting questions.

Proposed times (PDT): Mon 6/29 10:00-10:30, Tue 6/30 14:00-14:45, Wed 7/1 09:30-10:00. Please let me know what works and who else from Orchard should join (security, legal, procurement).

I've attached our Redwood Security Intake PDF to give your team a sense of questions we usually collect before kickoff.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

Best,

Thanks Tara — perfect. Matt, appreciate the questions. High-level proposal for scope to keep the kickoff focused:

Scope (proposed for kickoff):
- In scope: Redwood-hosted API endpoints used by Orchard, Redwood Console when used by your admins, and any direct S3 ingest paths (if you plan to push batches).
- Out of scope for initial kickoff: internal model training pipelines and our orchestration control plane (we can cover these later if needed).

Neha will lead questionnaire intake and can capture the gaps in the Orchard spreadsheet. For the kickoff we typically cover:
- Authentication & access control model (API keys, SSO options)
- Data residency & segregation (shared vs dedicated workloads)
- Encryption (in transit and at rest) and key management options
- Audit logging and retention windows
- Incident response & breach notification timelines

Quick clarifications that help prep the call:
1) Tara — can you confirm whether Orchard will require dedicated capacity (single-tenant GPU pools) or if multi-tenant hosted is acceptable for the pilot?
2) Matt — which systems should be explicitly listed as in-scope on your side (API, Console, S3 ingest, any logging sinks)?

We'll plan for Tue 6/30 14:00-14:45 PDT. I'll send a calendar invite and include a short pre-read (Neha will annotate Orchard_Security_Questionnaire_2026.xlsx with our intake notes).

Thanks all — Marissa

Thanks — confirmed for Tue 6/30 14:00 PDT. A few notes from security so Neha can prep: 

In-scope systems on Orchard side to call out:
- API endpoints used by our production service (api.orchardhealth.com -> Redwood API)
- Admin Console access for our ops team
- S3 ingestion buckets for batched historical ingest (s3://orchard-prod-ingest)

Controls/questions we need covered in kickoff:
- Are we able to get SOC 2 status and AOC? Is SOC 2 in-scope for the current contract?
- Encryption: we prefer customer-managed keys (KMS) for any PHI. Can Redwood support CMKs / HSM integration or do you offer dedicated capacity with KMS options?
- Data segregation: for pilot we want logical segregation; long-term we may need dedicated capacity — understanding cost delta and procurement timeline will help.
- Audit logs: retention minimum 1 year; need log streaming options (to our Splunk).

I'll attached a short list of required controls (see notes in the attached questionnaire). We'll aim to surface the non-negotiables on the kickoff and iterate on the questionnaire afterward.

See you on Tue — Matt

Matt Rivera
Head of Security | Orchard Health
matt.rivera@orchardhealth.com
